notes: prior to discussions on the next item.
South Fergus Secondary Plan
Report from B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development
B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development provided background and introduced Dave Aston, Partner, MHBC.

D. Aston provided an overview of the secondary plan framework, outlined other examples of secondary plans and indicated the proposed secondary plan addresses the mix, arrangement and density of land use, the collector road network, the size and location of parks and school sites and the location of major services. He noted the secondary plan implementation is accomplished through future zoning by-law amendments, plans of subdivision and site plan applications.

D. Aston outlined the key components undertaken with respect to the implementation of South Fergus Secondary Plan as well as the development of the Community Design Guidelines, including the design vision and principles. He responded to questions regarding policies to ensure compatibility between existing uses and new uses, reducing height of buildings and increasing density within low density areas, and the estimated community park size and location.

Brett Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development outlined the regulations regarding park dedication and the location of the various parks, open spaces and sports fields within the secondary plan. He also outlined the necessity for a mix of housing to mitigate the impact of development on prime agricultural lands and the use of low impact development such as rain and bioretention gardens, pervious pavement, green roofs and infiltration.

Colin Baker, Managing Director of Infrastructure Services indicated staff has initiated discussions with the Ministry of Transportation and has been invited to participate in the development of a highway access management plan that will review adjacent land uses, future traffic patterns and determine the future design of Highway 6.

D. Aston and staff responded to additional questions regarding planning for future cemeteries, stepping back levels on high density buildings, future health care needs, and potential incentives to encourage low impact development.
Mayor Watters called for a 5 minute recess and Councillor Wilton rejoined the meeting.

items.title: Amendments to the Procedure By-law 2021-31
notes: Report from K. O’Kane, Manager of Legislative Services & Municipal Clerk

Kerri O’Kane, Manager of Legislative Services & Municipal Clerk indicated consideration of the draft procedural by-law was deferred from the March 25th meeting. Staff is suggesting the following amendments to improve meeting efficiencies:
• updates to the electronic meetings provision and associated definitions to include hybrid participation;
• provisions regarding use of a consent agenda;
• changes to the Order of Business (inclusion of land acknowledgement, consent agenda);
• adjustment to the notice provision for advisory committees to align with current practices;
• reduction in time limit and restrictions on the number of opportunities a delegate may appear;
• adjustment to the meeting curfew;

Councillor Adams expressed concerns with the structure of two Council meetings per month and provided suggestions such as frequent information reports prior to major decisions, consideration for additional time to review the agendas and an awareness of upcoming projects.
